final_candidates.decision_summary: RING zinc-ligand cysteine substitution with the highest AlphaMissense LOF score (0.999) and the only RING cysteine mutant with nonzero homolog frequency, indicating folding-compatible evolutionary sampling. Best combined LOF/plausibility profile.
Canonical pathogenic RING allele disrupting the Zn2+-coordinating fold with near-maximal phenotype score (0.990) and rare but nonzero MSA tolerance. Slightly below C61R on evolutionary sampling.

Highest-spectrum RING zinc-finger cysteine substitution with phenotype 0.998 and strong MSA coverage (0.94) with near-zero mutant frequency, consistent with a disruptive but structurally viable allele.

stop_reason.detail: Top-3 ordering is stable across rounds; remaining near-saturated candidates differ only within AlphaMissense noise, so additional evidence would not change the outcome.

history.rationale: RING-domain zinc-coordinating cysteine; substitution to glycine disrupts Zn2+ binding and BARD1 interaction, abolishing ubiquitin ligase tumor-suppressor activity.
Cys61 coordinates Zn in the RING domain; disrupting a zinc-ligating cysteine should abolish E3 ubiquitin-ligase function while the domain remains largely structured.
Strong phenotype (0.990) but slightly below C61R and C39R; glycine may perturb local backbone more than an arginine substitution.
Canonical pathogenic RING allele with near-maximal phenotype score (0.990); MSA shows rare but nonzero G tolerance. Slightly below C61R due to lower evolutionary sampling.
Second RING Zn-ligating cysteine; tyrosine substitution is a classic BRCA1 loss-of-function missense variant while retaining overall fold of flanking regions.
Cys64 is the second RING zinc ligand; a bulky Tyr substitution is a classic LOF-style cysteine mutation predicted to be pathogenic.
Phenotype 0.993 at a third RING Zn-ligand cysteine; classic catastrophic-but-foldable zinc-finger disruption pattern.
Very high phenotype score (0.993) and zero homolog frequency at a conserved RING cysteine; stays competitive with the other RING alleles.
RING-domain cysteine; arginine abolishes zinc coordination and is a known pathogenic/LOF missense substitution.
Cys39 is the first RING Zn ligand; Arg substitution abolishes metal coordination and is a known pathogenic mechanism.
Near-maximal phenotype score (0.998) at the first RING zinc ligand; structurally a localized side-chain change unlikely to unfold the domain wholesale.
Highest phenotype z (0.998) with strong MSA coverage (0.94) and near-zero mutant frequency, consistent with a disruptive but well-aligned RING zinc-finger substitution.
BRCT domain residue in the phosphopeptide-binding pocket region; known severe missense change disrupting BRCT interactions.
Met1775 sits in the BRCT repeat interface critical for phosphopeptide binding; the classic M1775R founder mutation destabilizes the BRCT fold-function balance.
Phenotype 0.893 at the well-established BRCT M1775 hotspot, but lower than the RING cysteines; retained as backup.
Strong BRCT pathogenic variant but MSA coverage 0.04 makes evolutionary evidence inapplicable; phenotype (0.893) trails all four RING cysteine mutants, so demoted below Top-3.
BRCT domain conserved residue involved in phosphopeptide recognition; alanine substitution impairs Abraxas/CTIP binding.
BRCT-region substitution that may impair phosphopeptide recognition with limited global unfolding.
Ambiguous phenotype (0.444) and no mechanistic support for LOF; rejected.

rejection.reason: Ambiguous phenotype (0.444) and no mechanistic support for LOF; rejected.

history.rationale: Conserved BRCT-region residue contributing to partner binding surface; alanine substitution reduces tumor-suppressor interactions.
A conservative Ser-to-Ala change is unlikely to strongly abolish function; lowering confidence pending phenotype evidence.
Benign phenotype (0.337), conservative substitution; rejected.
Basic residue within BRCT domain; charge-reversal mutation perturbs the phosphopeptide-binding interface and suppressor function.
Charge reversal in the BRCT linker region is plausible but unvalidated; lowering confidence pending evidence.
BRCT-region phenotype 0.960, but no experimental support for K1702 being a critical BRCT residue; kept as backup diversifier.
High phenotype score (0.960) but MSA applicability is only 0.04 (9/211 coverage), so conservation evidence is uninformative and plausibility is modest; kept below RING alleles.
Alternative RING zinc-ligand substitution to diversify C61 alleles in case C61G scores poorly on evidence tools.

Highest phenotype score (0.999) among all candidates at a RING zinc-ligand position, directly aligned with the LOF reward. Low plausibility is expected and even consistent with strong functional disruption, not folding collapse.

RING zinc-ligand substitution with the highest AlphaMissense LOF score (0.999) and the only RING cysteine mutant with nonzero homolog frequency (0.166), indicating evolution has sampled R at this ligand position. Retained as top candidate.
Known pathogenic BRCT missense variant of the M1775 site; added as an alternative allele at this high-value position.
Similar to M1775R but slightly weaker phenotype; retained as alternate allele only.
Lowest phenotype score among BRCT candidates (0.879) with low PLM plausibility and no MSA coverage; dominated by M1775R and all RING alleles, so dropped from the pool.

rejection.reason: Lowest phenotype score among BRCT candidates (0.879) with low PLM plausibility and no MSA coverage; dominated by M1775R and all RING alleles, so dropped from the pool.
